**T4C — Compliant (at or above fallback; no redline proposed).**

- **Customer convenience right:** Section 12.2(a)(i) (p0488) gives Sanofi an unconditional right to terminate for convenience, in its entirety or country-by-country / Product-by-Product, with no lock-out period.
- **No penalty:** No early-termination fee or exit payment exists; the only post-termination money flow (Section 12.3(c)(ii)C) runs *to* us as royalties on Termination Products.
- **No Vendor convenience right:** RevMed's termination rights are all conditional/for-cause — material breach (12.2(b)), insolvency (12.2(c)), Competing Product (12.2(d)), cessation of development (12.2(e)). This meets the *preferred* element and exceeds the fallback's end-of-term/90-day allowance.
- **Noted, not flagged:** the 12.2(a)(i) notice periods are redacted (cannot confirm ≤30 days), and there is no pro-rata refund mechanic — upfront and milestone payments are expressly non-refundable, which is customary here as there are no prepaid service fees. Neither is a material fallback failure.
